candidate.answerReason: The straightaway lengths cancel, while the two semicircular ends add 2π·6 = 12π meters to the outer lap. Dividing this extra distance by 36 seconds gives π/3 meters per second, matching A.

methods.label: Compare the extra lap distance and time
methods.explanation:
Only the curved ends make the outside lap longer. The corresponding straightaways span the same end centers, so they have equal lengths. The track's width of \(6\) meters makes each outer semicircle's radius \(6\) meters greater than the inner radius.

[Figure 1](figures/2011_AMC_10B_Q12_question_fig1.svg)

The two semicircular ends together have the circumference of a full circle. If the inner radius is \(r>0\), the extra outside distance is
\[
2\pi(r+6)-2\pi r=12\pi
\]
meters.

Because Keiko walks at the same constant speed on both laps, this extra distance accounts for the extra \(36\) seconds. Her speed is therefore
\[
\frac{12\pi}{36}
=\boxed{\frac{\pi}{3}\text{ meters per second}},
\]
choice \(\text{A}\).
